# Browser extensions for QA

A few small extensions save a tester hours every week. They can change headers or mock an API without a proxy, run an accessibility scan in one click, paste boundary values into any field, capture a full-page screenshot, or produce a bug report with console and network logs attached. This chapter covers a short, proven set and explains how to install them without creating a security problem.

| Need | Extension | Browsers | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Modify headers, redirect, mock APIs | **Requestly** (alternative: ModHeader for headers only) | Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari (desktop app) | Free tier, paid plans |
| Accessibility scan | **axe DevTools**, **WAVE** | Chrome, Edge, Firefox | Free (axe has paid Pro features) |
| Edge-case test data | **Bug Magnet** | Chrome, Firefox | Free, open source |
| Full-page screenshot | **GoFullPage** | Chrome, Edge, Firefox | Free, premium editor |
| Bug report with logs | **Jam** | Chrome and Chromium browsers | Free tier, paid plans |
| Cookie editing and export | **Cookie-Editor** | Chrome, Firefox, Edge | Free |

```diagram
Separate browser profile for testing → install only from the official store → limit site access to test domains → use the extension (headers / mocks / a11y / data / capture) → turn it off when done → never on profiles with personal or production admin sessions
```

## Installing QA extensions safely: profiles, permissions and site access

Extensions can read and change every page they have access to. Treat them like software you install on a production server.

1. Create a **separate browser profile** for testing: Chrome profile icon → **Add** → **Continue without an account**. Name it `QA`. Keep personal email and banking out of it.
2. Install only from the official store (Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons, Edge Add-ons). Check the publisher, the number of users, recent updates and the requested permissions.
3. After installing, open `chrome://extensions` → the extension's **Details** → **Site access** and change *On all sites* to **On specific sites** (your test domains) or **On click**.
4. Pin the extensions you use often: puzzle icon in the toolbar → pin.
5. Turn extensions off when you're not using them. An active header or mock rule that you forgot about is a classic source of "can't reproduce" bugs.
6. Remember that extensions also run during automated or exploratory sessions in that profile, and they can change what the page does.

> **Caveat:** Many companies restrict extensions through browser policy. If an install button is greyed out, ask IT rather than trying to sideload.

## Requestly: modify headers, redirect environments and mock API responses

Requestly intercepts requests from inside the browser, so it needs no proxy and no certificates. It's a quick way to fake a feature flag header, point a page at a staging script, or return a stubbed API response.

**Add or override a header**

1. Install **Requestly** from the store and open it from the toolbar icon (or the Requestly web app).
2. Go to **HTTP Rules** → **New Rule** → **Modify Headers**.
3. Name the rule, for example `QA – feature flag new checkout`.
4. Define the condition: **URL** → **Contains** → `api.example.test`.
5. On the **Request Headers** tab, add a modification with the action **Add**, the header name `X-Feature-Flag` and the value `new-checkout`. Use the **Response Headers** tab to change response headers, for example to remove `Cache-Control`.
6. **Save** the rule and reload the page. Check the result in DevTools → Network → **Headers**.

![Requestly HTTP Rules screen with a new Modify Headers rule](https://mintcdn.com/requestly/7MWqoAA3Dhf9dCCV/images/modify-headers/e160e006-cd79-478c-bfd8-e8b73f02b59a.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=7MWqoAA3Dhf9dCCV&q=85&s=bed38e9858125139d9f8893a25357372 "Official Requestly documentation screenshot: creating a Modify Headers rule from HTTP Rules.")

**Other rule types QA uses**

- **Redirect Request**: load `app.js` from staging or `localhost` on the production page. Requestly's equivalent of Charles **Map Remote** / **Map Local**.
- **Modify API Response**: return a custom JSON body or status code for XHR/fetch calls. Use it to test empty states, errors and slow responses (delay).
- **Cancel Request**: block a call to test the failure path.
- **Delay Network Requests** and **Modify User Agents**: simulate slow endpoints or other clients.

> **Caveat:** Requestly rules stay active in every tab of that profile until you turn them off. Switch off the rules (or pause Requestly from its popup) when you finish.

**ModHeader** is a simpler alternative when you only need named header profiles (for example a `Authorization: Bearer ...` profile per test user). Requestly can import ModHeader profiles if you switch later.

## axe DevTools and WAVE: accessibility checks in the browser

Automated scanners find a large share of common accessibility defects, such as missing labels, low contrast, wrong ARIA and missing alt text. They can't judge everything, so combine them with keyboard and screen-reader checks.

**axe DevTools** (Deque, built on the open-source axe-core engine):

1. Install **axe DevTools – Web Accessibility Testing** from the store.
2. Open the page and open DevTools (`F12`). Find the **axe DevTools** tab, which may be behind the **»** overflow button.
3. Click **Full Page Scan** (scan all of my page). Use **Partial Page Scan** to check only one component, such as a modal.
4. Review the issues grouped by rule and severity (critical, serious, moderate, minor). Click **Highlight** to see the element on the page and **Inspect** to jump to it in Elements.
5. Each issue explains the WCAG rule and how to fix it. Copy that text into the bug report.

![axe DevTools browser extension welcome screen](https://www.deque.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/user-flow-analysis-splash-screen-1024x796.png "Deque product screenshot: the axe DevTools browser extension start screen.")

**WAVE** (WebAIM):

1. Install **WAVE Evaluation Tool**.
2. Run it on the page: click the WAVE toolbar icon, right-click → **WAVE this page**, or press `Ctrl+Shift+U` (Windows/Linux) / `Cmd+Shift+U` (macOS).
3. WAVE overlays icons on the page: red for errors, yellow for alerts, green for features, plus structure and ARIA markers. The sidebar groups them and has a **contrast** view.
4. Click the icon again or reload the page to remove the overlay.

![WAVE browser extension](https://wave.webaim.org/img/web/chromeExtension.png "Official WebAIM screenshot: the WAVE browser extension.")

> **QA tip:** WAVE runs entirely in your browser and sends nothing to a server, so it's safe on internal, logged-in and localhost pages. To scan local files or incognito windows, allow it in the extension settings first.

## Bug Magnet and fake-data fillers: edge-case input in one click

**Bug Magnet** (by Gojko Adzic) adds a right-click menu with values that tend to break software.

1. Install **Bug Magnet** for Chrome or Firefox.
2. Right-click inside any input, textarea or editable element → **Bug Magnet**.
3. Choose a category and a value: very long strings, Unicode and emoji, right-to-left text, whitespace-only text, SQL- and HTML-like strings, boundary numbers, invalid and unusual email addresses, names with apostrophes, and so on.
4. The value is inserted into the field. Submit the form and check the validation message, the stored value and how it's displayed elsewhere.
5. You can extend the menu with your own configuration file, for example product-specific IDs or locale-specific formats.

Typical checks: the UI shows a clear validation error, nothing is cut off or overflows, the API rejects the value with `400` instead of failing with `500`, and the value is escaped when shown back (no script runs).

For filling long registration forms, use a **fake-data form filler** extension. It fills every field with realistic random data, so you spend your time on the field under test rather than on typing.

> **Caveat:** Only use injection-style values against systems you're allowed to test. Run them on staging, not on production or third-party sites.

## Screenshots, recordings and bug reports: GoFullPage, Jam and built-in tools

**GoFullPage** captures an entire scrolling page as one image:

1. Install **GoFullPage – Full Page Screen Capture**.
2. Open the page and click the camera icon, or press `Alt+Shift+P`.
3. Wait while it scrolls and stitches the page, then download the result as PNG or PDF.

**Jam** creates a shareable bug report with the technical context attached:

1. Install **Jam** and sign in.
2. Reproduce the bug, then click the Jam icon and choose a screenshot, a screen recording, or **Instant Replay** (the last moments before you clicked).
3. Jam attaches the console logs, network requests, browser and device information and the user steps, and gives you a link. Integrations can push it into Jira, Linear, GitHub and other trackers.
4. Review the report before sharing. Blur anything sensitive and remember that it includes network data.

**No extension at all:** DevTools' Command Menu (`Ctrl+Shift+P`) → **Capture full size screenshot** or **Capture node screenshot**. Windows `Win+Shift+S` and macOS `Cmd+Shift+5` handle region screenshots and screen recording.

> **Caveat:** Bug-report extensions upload what they capture to their cloud. Check your company's policy before using them on internal or customer-data systems.

## Cookie-Editor: inspect, edit and export cookies quickly

DevTools' **Application → Cookies** covers most cookie work. **Cookie-Editor** is faster for one specific job: moving or reproducing a session.

1. Install **Cookie-Editor** and click its icon on the site under test. All cookies for the current tab are listed.
2. Click a cookie to edit its value, expiry or flags, or use **+** to add one.
3. Click **Export** to copy all cookies as JSON (or in Netscape or header format) to the clipboard. **Import** loads them back, for example into a clean QA profile to reproduce a state.
4. Use the delete-all button to start from a clean session.

> **Caveat:** Exported cookies are your logged-in session. Anyone who has them can act as you. Use them only with test accounts, and never paste them into tickets or chats.

## Cheat sheet

| Task | Extension and action |
| --- | --- |
| Add a header to every API call | Requestly → HTTP Rules → Modify Headers |
| Load a script from staging | Requestly → Redirect Request |
| Stub an API response or status | Requestly → Modify API Response |
| Header profiles per user | ModHeader |
| Accessibility scan in DevTools | axe DevTools → Full Page Scan |
| Visual accessibility overlay | WAVE → `Ctrl+Shift+U` / `Cmd+Shift+U` |
| Boundary and Unicode values | Right-click a field → Bug Magnet |
| Full-page screenshot | GoFullPage (`Alt+Shift+P`) or DevTools → Capture full size screenshot |
| Bug report with logs | Jam → Instant Replay |
| Move a session between profiles | Cookie-Editor → Export / Import |
| Restrict an extension | `chrome://extensions` → Details → Site access |

## Summary

- Use a separate test profile, install only from official stores, and limit site access to your test domains.
- Requestly changes headers, redirects scripts and mocks API responses inside the browser, with no proxy or certificates needed.
- axe DevTools and WAVE catch common accessibility issues quickly. Keyboard and screen-reader checks are still needed.
- Bug Magnet speeds up negative input testing. GoFullPage, Jam and the built-in screenshot tools make evidence complete. Cookie-Editor moves sessions, so treat exported cookies as secrets.
